name: ASG-00032
title: Writing Task
question:
Write 120–150 words about a moment you’ve shared with a friend. Use past simple and past continuous

EXAMPLE: Last summer, I went (PS) to the beach with my friend Emma. The sun was shining (PC), and the waves were crashing (PC) gently on the shore. While we were walking (PC) along the sand, we found (PS) a small crab near the water. Emma was laughing (PC) because it kept running (PC) away from us. We decided (PS) to build a sandcastle together. As we were building (PC) it, a strong wave came (PS) and washed (PS) part of our castle away. Instead of being upset, we were laughing (PC) and helped (PS) each other rebuild it. That day, I realized (PS) how much fun it is to share little moments with friends.

name: ASG-00102
title: Writing task - lesson two
question:
B1 Writing Assignment – “My Cooking or Baking Experience”

Instructions:

  1. Write about a time you cooked or baked something.

  2. Use past simple for completed actions and past continuous for actions happening at the same time.

  3. Use time sequencers like: first, then, next, after that, finally.

  4. Include at least 5–7 sentences.

  5. Try to describe:

    • What you were cooking or baking

    • Who you were with

    • What steps you did

    • How you felt at the end

Example Starter:

  • First, I preheated the oven and gathered all the ingredients.

  • While I was mixing the dough, my friend was cracking the eggs.

  • Next, we added the chocolate chips and folded the mixture gently.

name: ASG-00459
title: Lesson two, part five
question:
Task:

Imagine you were part of a team working on a project or event at your company (real or imaginary). Write a short report or email to your manager describing what happened.

Instructions:

  1. Write 150–200 words.

  2. Use time sequencers to show the order of events. (e.g., First, Next, After that, Finally)

  3. Use Past Simple for short, finished actions and Past Continuous for actions that were happening at the same time.

  4. Include at least 5 vocabulary words from this lesson, such as:

    • proposal

    • deadline

    • client

    • approve

    • discuss

    • feedback

    • schedule

    • deliver

  5. Your email or report should clearly describe:

    • What your team did

    • Any problems or challenges

    • How you solved them

    • The final outcome

name: ASG-00648
title: Lesson six, part five: Writing assignment
question:
Writing Task – Past Perfect Continuous (Networking Theme)

Instructions:

Write a short paragraph about a networking event you attended (real or imagined).

Examples of things to include:

  • How you prepared for the event

  • How long you had been practicing introductions or presentations

  • How attendees or organizers had been preparing beforehand

  • Any ongoing actions that affected the outcome of the event

Example sentence:

“I had been preparing questions for potential partners for several days before the networking event, which made it easier to start conversations.”

✅ Tip for students:

  • Use the structure: subject + had been + verb-ing

  • Think about duration or ongoing actions before the main past event

  • Connect the preparation to a result if possible

name: ASG-00931
title: A2 - Lesson One: Written assignment
question:
Written Assignment – “My Daily Routine”Instructions for Students:

  1. Write one page (5–8 sentences) about your daily routine.

  2. Use Present Simple for habits, routines, likes, and facts.

  3. Include signal words: usually, sometimes, always, every day, after, then, first.

  4. Use at least 5 new vocabulary words from our reading and vocabulary tables (e.g., cafeteria, tasks, classmates, organized, active).

  5. Check your verbs: remember he/she/it adds -s/-es.

Questions to Guide You

  • What time do you wake up?

  • What do you do first in the morning?

  • How do you go to school/work?

  • What do you do during breaks or free time?

  • What do you eat for breakfast, lunch, or dinner?

  • What activities do you do after school/work?

  • What time do you go to bed?

  • Why do you like your routine?

name: ASG-00127
title: B1 Lesson 3 - Speaking
question:
NOTE: For the speaking tests you must record your answer separately then upload it as a URL. 

Speaking Assignment – Sports and Present Perfect

Objective:

Practice talking about your experience playing sport using the Present Perfect tense.

Instructions:

  1. Think about a sport you play or enjoy watching.

  2. Prepare answers to the questions below.

  3. Use full sentences and try to use Present Perfect wherever possible.

  4. Speak for 1–2 minutes about your sport experience.

Prompts:

  1. What sport have you recently started playing or watching?

  2. How often have you practiced or played this sport?

  3. Have you improved any skills in this sport?

  4. Have you played any matches or competitions? How did they go?

  5. Have you ever joined a club, team, or group for this sport?

  6. Have you learned anything important about teamwork or training?

name: ASG-00153
title: B1 Lesson 4
question:
Writing Assignment: Your museum or excursion experience

Instructions for Students:

  1. Think about a recent trip, museum visit, or day out that you have taken.

  2. Write a short article or report (about 120–180 words)

  3. Include the following in your writing:

    • Include sentences using Present Perfect to talk about:

      • Experiences (I have never…, I have just…)

      • Actions that affect the present (We have already…, I haven’t… yet)

      • Repeated actions or habits (I have visited… several times)

    • At least three adverbs commonly used with Present Perfect (just, already, yet, ever, never, since, for)

    • At least five new words from the vocabulary list: exhibition, renovation, layout, gallery, sketch, curious, crowded, challenging, inspiring, exhibit, appreciate, reflect.

  4. Use paragraphs and write clearly, as if you are reporting for other students.

name: ASG-00172
title: Lesson 5 - Speaking assignment
question:

Instructions:

  1. Think of a trip or journey you have taken, or imagine one.

  2. Prepare a 1–2 minute recording where you describe the trip.

  3. Include:

    • Past Perfect to show what happened before other actions

      • Example: “I had already packed my suitcase before I left home.”

    • Adverbs like already, just, yet if possible

    • Lesson vocabulary (at least 5 words): flight status, gate, boarding pass, exhausted, restless, delay, captain, announcement, perspective, mix, awake

Prompts to guide your speaking:

  • Did anything unexpected happen? What had caused it?

  • How did you feel during the journey?

  • What had you planned or prepared before the trip?

  • What happened first, and what happened after?

name: ASG-00768
title: Lesson eight, part five: speaking assignment
question:
NOTE: For the speaking tests you must record your answer separately then upload it as a URL. 

Task 1: Individual Speaking (2–3 minutes)

Instructions:

  1. Imagine you are the manager for the company conference.

  2. Using the timeline as inspiration, describe:

    • Your plans for the event (use going to or present continuous).

    • Predictions about the conference outcome (will).

    • Actions that will be completed before the event (future perfect).

Example Prompts:

  • “Tomorrow, the team is meeting to discuss the keynote speaker.”

  • “By the end of February, we will have sent all invitations.”

  • “We are going to organize a rehearsal for the presentations.”

  • “I think the conference will be very successful.”

title: B1, L1: Speaking Task

name: ASG-00521
title: Writing Assignment: Project Reflection Report
question:
Writing Assignment: Project Reflection Report

Task: Write a short report (150–200 words) reflecting on recent projects or work initiatives in your team or company. Focus on what has been achieved so far using the Present Perfect. Include at least 3 adverbs: just, already, yet, ever, never.

Instructions:

  1. Title: Give your report a clear title, e.g., “Project Achievements This Year”

  2. Introduction: Briefly explain the purpose of the report.

  3. Achievements and Results: Describe what your team or company has done. Use Present Perfect for completed or ongoing actions.

  4. Challenges and Improvements: Mention any challenges and how they have been addressed.

  5. Conclusion: Summarize the impact of these projects and any next steps.

Example sentence starters:

  • “Our team has completed several important projects this year.”

  • “We have already implemented new strategies to improve efficiency.”

  • “Some departments haven’t finished their training yet.”

  • “We have just received feedback from clients.”

Suggested Vocabulary:

  • initiative

  • achievement

  • innovation

  • collaboration

  • strategy

  • milestone

  • improvement

  • impact

name: ASG-00554
title: Lesson five, speaking
question:
NOTE: For the speaking tests you must record your answer separately then upload it as a URL. 

Instructions:

  1. Imagine you were at a central station during a train delay as described in the article.

  2. Speak aloud for 2–3 minutes, describing the situation.

  3. Make sure to include:

    • Events that had happened before the delay announcement.

    • How passengers and staff had reacted.

    • What you personally had done while waiting.

    • How the situation was finally resolved.

Prompts to Guide You

  • What had happened before you arrived at the station?

  • Which problems had passengers experienced before the announcement?

  • How had engineers fixed the signalling problem?

  • What had you done to manage the delay?

  • How did the delay make people feel, and why?

Tips for Success

  • Use Past Perfect for the action that happened first:

    • “By the time I arrived, the staff had already made the announcement.”

    • “I had checked the departure board before going to the platform.”

  • Use Past Simple for the action that happened later:

    • “The train finally left at 7:20 p.m.”

  • Include time markers to clarify the order of events:

    • “Earlier in the evening,” “by the time,” “before the train moved again”

  • Speak clearly and try to link sentences naturally.

Steps to Upload Your Audio

  1. Log in to the platform

  2. Click Upload or Add File.

  3. Select your audio file from your device.

  4. Click save

  5. Check that your audio plays correctly after uploading.

name: ASG-00799
title: Lesson nine, part five: writing assignment
question:
Writing Assignment – “A Small Mistake” Task

Write a short story (120–180 words) about a time when:

  • You made a small mistake

  • There was a misunderstanding

  • Something did not go as planned

Your story can be real or imaginary.

You must include: At least:

  • 2 words with prefixes (e.g. misunderstand, recheck, reschedule, unhappy)

  • 3 words with suffixes (e.g. embarrassed, helpful, kindness, nervousness, memorable)

name: ASG-00830
title: Lesson ten, part five: speaking assignment
question:
NOTE: For the speaking tests you must record your answer separately then upload it as a URL. 

You are a sales assistant preparing for a busy Spring Sale at your store. You have read the manager’s memo and need to explain your plan, predict problems, and give advice.

Instructions:

  1. Prepare a 2–3 minute spoken report to your manager or a colleague.

  2. Include the following:

A. Planning Tasks

  • Explain how you will organize the store using conditionals.

    • Example: “If we arrange the displays carefully, customers will find products easily.”

  • Mention what you will do if stock runs low.

    • Example: “If stock is low, I should reorder immediately.”

B. Problem Prediction

  • Predict possible issues and how to handle them using modals + conditionals.

    • Example: “If a customer complains, I might offer a polite solution.”

    • Example: “If push comes to shove, I could help at the checkout.”

C. Reflect and Conclude

  • End by summarizing your plan:

    • Example: “If all goes well, the sale will run smoothly, but if worst comes to worst, I will handle the problems professionally.”

name: ASG-01053
title: IELTS Gen Writing Mock Test 1 Task 2
question:

than previous generations did.

name: ASG-01055
title: IELTS Gen Writing Mock Test 2 Task 1
question:
You have recently moved to a new neighbourhood. You have met your neighbour a few times but do not know them well. You have noticed that their car is sometimes parked in a way that blocks your driveway.

Write a letter to your neighbour. In your letter:

  •  introduce yourself and explain the situation

  •  describe the problems this causes for you

•  suggest a practical solution

Write at least 150 words.

You do NOT need to write any addresses.

name: ASG-01056
title: IELTS Gen Writing Mock Test 2 Task 2
question:
In many countries, young people are finding it increasingly difficult to afford to buy their own home. House prices have risen far faster than wages, making home ownership seem out of reach for many.

What are the causes of this problem and what measures could governments and individuals take to address it?

Write at least 250 words.

name: ASG-01050
title: IELTS Ac Writing Mock Test 1 Task 2
question:
Some people believe that university education should be free for all
students, funded entirely by the government. Others argue that students should contribute towards the cost of their own education through tuition fees.

In your opinion, should universitities be funded by the gouvernment or by students? You should give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own experience or knowledge to support your response.

Write a minimum of 250 words.

name: ASG-01059
title: IELTS Ac Writing Mock Test 2 Task 2
question:

name: ASG-01052
title: IELTS Gen Writing Mock Test 1 Task 1
question:
You recently booked a holiday through a travel agency. When you arrived at the hotel, you found that it was significantly different from what was described on the agency's website.

Write a letter to the travel agency manager. In your letter:

  •  describe what the website said about the hotel

  •  explain how the hotel was different from the description

  •  say what action you would like the agency to take

Write at least 150 words.

You do NOT need to write any addresses.

name: ASG-01351
title: A2 Lesson 6, speaking assignment
question:
Speaking Assignment: Choosing the Best Workplace

NOTE: For the speaking tests you must record your answer separately then upload it as a URL. 

Task

You are starting a new job. You have two workplaces to choose from (for example: two offices, two meeting rooms, or two coworking spaces).

Your task is to compare the two options and decide which one is best for you.

Step 1: Prepare (2–3 minutes)

Think about these ideas:


  • size (big / small)


  • price (cheap / expensive)


  • location (near / far)


  • noise (quiet / busy)


  • comfort (comfortable / not comfortable)

Step 2: Speak (1–2 minutes)

Talk about both options and use comparatives and superlatives.

Try to include:


  • at least 3 comparatives (e.g. bigger than, cheaper than)


  • at least 1 superlative (e.g. the best, the cheapest)

question:

name: ASG-01322
title: A2 Lesson four - writing assignment
question:
Task:

Write a short paragraph (8–10 sentences) about a grocery trip, a picnic, or preparing food and drinks. Use countable and uncountable nouns correctly.

Instructions:


  1. Start by making a small shopping list in your mind or on paper. Include at least 5 items, some countable, some uncountable.


    • Example: apples, milk, chocolate, bread, juice.


  2. Describe what you bought or prepared. Use containers, measure words, and quantifiers.


    • Examples: a loaf of bread, a few apples, a bottle of milk, some chocolate, a jar of juice.


  3. Use at least 2 sentences with countable nouns and 2 sentences with uncountable nouns.


  4. Include a small problem or surprise if you want - like forgetting something, or finding a basket of food (optional).


  5. End with a sentence about how it felt — happy, excited, or funny.

name: ASG-01387
title: A2 Lesson 7
question:
Task: Write a short paragraph (50–70 words) about a day at your workplace, a school, a café, or another place you know. Use at least 4 different modal verbs (must, should, can, might, have to, don’t have to, mustn’t).

Steps:

  3. Include advice or suggestions using “should.”


  4. Include possibility or permission using “might” or “can.”

name: ASG-01423
title: A2 Lesson 8
question:
Speaking Assignment: My Future Plans (Individual)Objective

Speak for 1–2 minutes about your future using:

  • will

  • going to

  • might

Task

Prepare a short talk about your future plans.

You should include:

  • 1 plan (going to)

  • 1 prediction or decision (will)

  • 1 possibility (might)

Guiding Questions

You can use these ideas to help you:


  • What are you going to do this weekend?


  • What are you going to do next week?


  • What will you do after this class?


  • What will your life be like in the future?


  • What might you do in your free time?

name: ASG-01453
title: A2 part  nine
question:
Write a short paragraph (80–100 words) about communication in your daily life.

You should include:


  • How you communicate every day (phone, messages, social media, etc.)

    What you use technology for


  • One advantage of technology


  • One disadvantage of too much technology

    At least 2 passive voice sentences

  • Useful ideas / phrases


  • I use my phone to…


  • Messages are sent…


  • Social media is used to…


  • Information is shared…


  • Apps are created to…


  • Too much time is spent online…

  • Success criteria

    ✔ Clear ideas

    ✔ Simple vocabulary

    ✔ At least 2 passive sentences

    ✔ 80–100 words
